Method of Attack: Infects Linux servers and Linux-based IoT devices
Carries out dictionary (brute-force) attacks against other devices via SSH
Downloads its binary to new hosts after successful brute-force
Starts a local web server on port 61314 for self-update and self-upgrade
Reports host details back to C&C server
Uses command and control server to receive configuration and user-pass combos
Discoverer: ESET researchers Peter Kálnai and Michal Malik
Attack Vector: SSH brute-force attacks using username and password combinations
Indicators of Compromise: Folders named ".javaxxx", ".swap", or "kworker" created by malware
Local web server running on port 61314
Connection to command and control server
Reports including chip architecture, config version, device hardware details, IP address
